note: Declarative species surface profiles (CLAUDE.md §41B, 'Every Hunt-eligible species has a map'). Each profile quotes the habitat statement North Ground has already published for the species, verbatim, with that statement's sources; the builder refuses a profile whose quote is not in the published profile. The CLASSES are North Ground's reading of that statement onto the land-cover groups — categorical, never fitted, never density. Read by scripts/build-range-habitat-surfaces.mjs.

SMALL_GAME.why: Home ranges of rabbits, hares and squirrels are small; a record speaks for little ground around it.

FURBEARER.why: Mid-sized mammals range further than small game but hold defined territories.

BIG_GAME.why: Ungulates move seasonally across tens of kilometres.

LOCAL_BIG_GAME.why: Herds confined to particular mountains, ranches or released populations: a record speaks for the ground near it, not for a region.

LARGE_CARNIVORE.why: Large carnivores hold territories of hundreds of square kilometres.

ARCTIC.why: Few people record anything in the Arctic, so records are sparse relative to the animals; the reach is wider and the confidence lower.

WATERFOWL_SEASON.why: Migratory birds in the hunting season, from records made in the hunting season; flocks move among stopovers.

SEA_DUCK_SEASON.why: Sea ducks in the hunting season concentrate along coasts and large lakes, from records made in the hunting season.

MARSH_BIRD_SEASON.why: Secretive marsh birds, from records made in the hunting season.

species:aberts-squirrel.habitatStatement: Ponderosa pine forests of the southwestern United States, including Arizona, New Mexico and Colorado.
species:aberts-squirrel.reading: Needleleaf forest is core; other forest is secondary; open ground is not habitat.

species:american-badger.habitatStatement: Open grassland, prairie, farmland and sagebrush with soils suited to digging.
species:american-badger.reading: Grassland is core; farmland and sagebrush (shrub) are strong; open woodland is marginal; closed forest, water and towns are not habitat. Soils are not in the land cover and are not modelled.

species:american-bison.habitatStatement: Managed herds on prairie and parkland; free-ranging herds are limited and mostly on public or protected lands.
species:american-bison.reading: Prairie grassland is core; parkland (open broadleaf woodland) and shrubland are strong; the range is drawn tightly because herds are local.

species:american-black-bear.habitatStatement: Forested areas provide seasonally changing foods, refuge and den sites. Habitat value depends on the diversity and timing of food, security cover and denning opportunities.
species:american-black-bear.reading: Broadleaf and mixed forest (the most varied seasonal foods) are core; needleleaf forest and shrub are strong; wetland is moderate; open and farmed land is marginal.

species:american-marten.habitatStatement: Coniferous and mixed forests with structural cover across northern North America.
species:american-marten.reading: Closed coniferous and mixed forest (structural cover) is core; open or unclassified forest is strong; broadleaf forest is moderate.

species:american-mink.habitatStatement: Shorelines, marshes and wooded waterways across North America.
species:american-mink.reading: Tied to water: a cell is judged first on its water and wetland (required), then on its land — marsh core, wooded land strong.

gbifName.name: Neovison vison
gbifName.why: GBIF's backbone has no entry for Neogale vison (the 2021 genus revision) and files American mink under its former name, Neovison vison: the same animal, and the catalogue keeps the current name.

species:american-red-squirrel.habitatStatement: Coniferous and mixed forests across northern North America.
species:american-red-squirrel.reading: Coniferous and mixed forest are core; other forest strong; broadleaf moderate.

species:arctic-fox.habitatStatement: Arctic tundra and coastal environments north of the treeline.
species:arctic-fox.reading: Tundra (moss, lichen, grass) is core; bare ground and tundra shrub are strong; forest is not habitat, which keeps the surface north of the treeline.

species:arctic-hare.habitatStatement: Treeless Arctic tundra and rocky polar landscapes.
species:arctic-hare.reading: Tundra and rocky bare ground are core; grass and shrub tundra strong; forest is not habitat.

species:axis-deer.habitatStatement: Introduced to Texas and Hawaii; open woodland and savanna-like ranchland.
species:axis-deer.reading: Open woodland and shrub savanna are core; grassland strong; closed forest moderate. Hawaii lies outside North Ground's continental foundation and is not drawn.

species:barbary-sheep.habitatStatement: Introduced to rugged arid country of Texas and New Mexico.
species:barbary-sheep.reading: Rugged terrain is required (local relief); arid shrub and bare ground are core, grassland strong.

species:beaver.habitatStatement: Ponds, lakes, rivers and wetlands where woody vegetation is available.
species:beaver.reading: Water is required; woody vegetation beside it decides the rest — broadleaf, mixed and shrub (willow, aspen) core, needleleaf strong.

species:bighorn-sheep.habitatStatement: Steep rocky terrain, alpine meadows and desert mountains of western North America.
species:bighorn-sheep.reading: Steep terrain is required (local relief); rock, alpine meadow and mountain shrub are core; open forest strong.

species:black-scoter.habitatStatement: Breeds in northern wetlands; winters on coastal ocean waters.
species:black-scoter.reading: In the hunting season: coastal sea within 20 km of land is core; large inland water is moderate; land is not habitat.

species:black-tailed-jackrabbit.habitatStatement: Deserts, grasslands and farmland of the western United States.
species:black-tailed-jackrabbit.reading: Desert shrub and grassland are core; farmland and bare desert strong; woodland marginal.

species:bobcat.habitatStatement: Forest, brush, rocky country and agricultural edges across southern Canada and the United States.
species:bobcat.reading: Forest and brush are core; rocky ground strong; farmland and grassland moderate (edges); towns marginal.

species:brant.habitatStatement: Arctic tundra breeding areas and marine coasts rich in eelgrass or algae outside breeding season.
species:brant.reading: In the hunting season: coastal sea within 10 km of land is core; coastal marsh strong; other water moderate. Eelgrass beds are not in the land cover and are not modelled.

species:brown-bear.habitatStatement: Alaska and western or northern Canada in habitats from coast to alpine and tundra.
species:brown-bear.reading: A generalist from coast to alpine: tundra, shrub, grass, open and needleleaf forest are all strong, none singled out as core; farmland, towns and open water are not habitat.

species:brush-rabbit.habitatStatement: Dense brush and chaparral of the Pacific coast from Oregon to Baja California.
species:brush-rabbit.reading: Brush and chaparral (shrub) are core; open woodland strong; grass and closed forest moderate.

species:cackling-goose.habitatStatement: Tundra breeding grounds and open fields, wetlands and coasts during migration and winter.
species:cackling-goose.reading: In the hunting season: open fields and wetlands are core; grassland, open water and coastal sea within 10 km of land strong.

species:canada-lynx.habitatStatement: Boreal forest strongly associated with snowshoe hare populations.
species:canada-lynx.reading: Boreal needleleaf and mixed forest are core; other forest and regenerating shrub strong; wetland moderate. Snowshoe hare abundance is not modelled.

species:caribou.habitatStatement: Tundra and boreal landscapes; population and ecotype distinctions are important.
species:caribou.reading: Lichen tundra is core; open conifer, tundra shrub, grass and peatland strong; closed conifer moderate. Herds and ecotypes are not distinguished — hunting is by herd and the zone card governs.

species:collared-peccary.habitatStatement: Deserts, brushland and oak woodland of Texas, New Mexico and Arizona.
species:collared-peccary.reading: Brushland is core; open (oak) woodland and bare desert strong; grassland and closed woodland moderate.

species:common-eider.habitatStatement: Northern coasts; breeds on islands and coastal tundra and winters on cold ocean waters.
species:common-eider.reading: In the hunting season: coastal sea within 15 km of land is core; land is not habitat.

species:coyote.habitatStatement: Highly adaptable across forest, farmland, prairie and urban-edge landscapes.
species:coyote.reading: A generalist: farmland, prairie, shrub and open woodland strong; closed forest, towns and wetland moderate; none singled out as core.

species:dall-sheep.habitatStatement: Alpine and subalpine mountains of Alaska, Yukon, northern British Columbia and the Northwest Territories.
species:dall-sheep.reading: Mountain terrain is required (local relief); alpine grass, tundra, rock and shrub are core; subalpine open forest strong.

species:desert-cottontail.habitatStatement: Arid grassland, desert and brush of the western and southwestern United States.
species:desert-cottontail.reading: Arid grass and brush are core; bare desert strong; farmland edges moderate.

species:eastern-cottontail.habitatStatement: Brushy fields, hedgerows and suburban edges in eastern and central North America.
species:eastern-cottontail.reading: Brush is core, and ground where fields meet woodland (an edge) is core; fields strong; suburbs moderate.

species:eastern-gray-squirrel.habitatStatement: Deciduous and mixed woodland, parks and urban areas in eastern North America.
species:eastern-gray-squirrel.reading: Deciduous and mixed woodland are core; other woodland and parks/towns strong; conifer moderate.

species:eastern-wolf.habitatStatement: Forested landscapes of central Ontario and neighbouring Québec; taxonomy and hybrid ancestry are treated differently by authorities.
species:eastern-wolf.reading: Forest is core; wetland and shrub moderate; open and farmed land marginal. Records under this name depend on how each contributor treats the taxon.

species:elk.habitatStatement: Western forests, foothills and grasslands, plus some restored eastern populations.
species:elk.reading: Forest, grassland and shrub are all strong, none singled out as core; farmland is moderate.

species:fallow-deer.habitatStatement: Introduced; parkland, farms and ranches, with free-ranging populations in limited areas.
species:fallow-deer.reading: Parkland (open woodland) and grassland are strong; farms and closed woodland moderate; the range is drawn tightly because populations are local.

species:fisher.habitatStatement: Mature and regenerating forest across northern North America.
species:fisher.reading: Closed (mature) forest is core; open and unclassified forest strong; regenerating shrub moderate.

species:fox-squirrel.habitatStatement: Open woodland, woodlots and river bottoms of the eastern and central United States and far southern Canada.
species:fox-squirrel.reading: Open broadleaf and mixed woodland are core; closed broadleaf woodland strong; woodlots in farmland (an edge of woodland and field) strong.

species:gray-fox.habitatStatement: Woodland and brushy habitat in the southern part of Canada and much of the United States.
species:gray-fox.reading: Brush and broadleaf or mixed woodland are core; conifer strong; farmland and grass moderate.

species:gray-wolf.habitatStatement: Forests, tundra, mountains and open country across much of Canada and Alaska.
species:gray-wolf.reading: A generalist: forest, tundra, open country and mountain ground are all strong, none singled out as core; farmland and towns marginal.

species:greater-white-fronted-goose.habitatStatement: Arctic tundra in summer and wetlands or agricultural fields during migration and winter.
species:greater-white-fronted-goose.reading: In the hunting season: wetlands and farm fields are core; open water and grass strong.

species:harlequin-duck.habitatStatement: Breeds on fast mountain streams and winters along rocky coastal surf.
species:harlequin-duck.reading: In the hunting season: sea within 5 km of land (the surf line) is core; rocky shores are not separable in the land cover.

species:king-eider.habitatStatement: Breeds in the High Arctic and winters on northern ocean waters.
species:king-eider.reading: In the hunting season: northern ocean within 30 km of land is core; land is not habitat.

species:king-rail.habitatStatement: Freshwater and brackish marshes of the eastern and central United States.
species:king-rail.reading: Marsh is required: a cell is judged on its share of herbaceous wetland.

species:long-tailed-duck.habitatStatement: Breeds on Arctic tundra ponds and winters on large lakes and coastal waters.
species:long-tailed-duck.reading: In the hunting season: coastal sea within 30 km of land is core; large lakes strong.

species:montezuma-quail.habitatStatement: Grassy oak and pine woodland of southeastern Arizona, southwestern New Mexico and west Texas.
species:montezuma-quail.reading: Open (grassy) oak and pine woodland is core; grass, shrub and other woodland strong; closed forest moderate.

species:moose.habitatStatement: Moose need young forest and shrubs for browse together with mature cover for shelter. Aquatic feeding areas, mineral licks and calving sites are important localized features.
species:moose.reading: Mixed and broadleaf forest and shrub (browse beside cover) are core; needleleaf forest and wetland (aquatic feeding) strong; open water moderate; farmland marginal. Mineral licks and calving sites are not in the land cover and are not modelled.

species:mountain-cottontail.habitatStatement: Sagebrush, brush and mountain forest openings of the interior West and southern interior British Columbia.
species:mountain-cottontail.reading: Sagebrush and brush are core; grass and open mountain forest strong; closed conifer moderate.

species:mountain-goat.habitatStatement: Steep cliffs and alpine terrain of western mountains from Alaska and Yukon to the northern Rockies.
species:mountain-goat.reading: Steep terrain is required (local relief, set higher than for sheep); rock, alpine grass, tundra and shrub are core; snowfields moderate; forest marginal.

species:mountain-lion.habitatStatement: Mountains, forests, canyons and brush of western North America, with a small population in Florida.
species:mountain-lion.reading: Forest, brush and broken rocky ground are all strong, none singled out as core; grass and wetland (Florida) moderate.

species:mule-deer.habitatStatement: Western shrublands, mountains, forests and open country.
species:mule-deer.reading: Shrubland, forest and open country are all strong, none singled out as core; farmland and bare mountain ground moderate.

species:muskox.habitatStatement: Arctic tundra of Canada, Greenland and Alaska.
species:muskox.reading: Tundra (moss, lichen, grass, low shrub) is core; wet tundra and bare ground strong; forest is not habitat.

species:muskrat.habitatStatement: Marshes, ponds, streams and ditches across most of North America.
species:muskrat.reading: Water or marsh is required; marsh is core, ponds strong, farmland ditches moderate.

species:nilgai.habitatStatement: Introduced to the coastal plains and brushland of south Texas.
species:nilgai.reading: Brushland is core; coastal grass plain and open woodland strong; farmland moderate.

species:north-american-river-otter.habitatStatement: Rivers, lakes, marshes and coastal waters across much of North America.
species:north-american-river-otter.reading: Water, marsh or coastal sea is required; forested shores strong, open shores moderate.

species:nutria.habitatStatement: Introduced; marshes and waterways of the southern United States and the Pacific Northwest.
species:nutria.reading: Marsh or waterway is required; marsh is core, water strong, wet farmland moderate.

species:polar-bear.habitatStatement: Arctic sea ice and coasts of Canada, Alaska and Greenland.
species:polar-bear.reading: Coastal Arctic sea within 50 km of land is core (sea ice is seasonal and is not in the land cover, so the sea it forms on stands for it); coastal land is marginal.

species:pronghorn.habitatStatement: Open prairie, sagebrush and semi-arid grassland of western North America.
species:pronghorn.reading: Grassland and sagebrush are core; farmland and bare semi-desert moderate; woodland marginal; closed forest is not habitat.

species:purple-gallinule.habitatStatement: Southern freshwater marshes with floating vegetation.
species:purple-gallinule.reading: Freshwater marsh is required: a cell is judged on its share of herbaceous wetland; open water beside it moderate.

gbifName.name: Porphyrio martinica
gbifName.why: GBIF's backbone spells the species Porphyrio martinica, and its own match service offers that record for Porphyrio martinicus: the same species under the other spelling of the epithet.

species:raccoon.habitatStatement: Woodland, wetlands, farmland and urban areas, usually near water or cover.
species:raccoon.reading: A generalist near water or cover: woodland, wetland, farmland and towns are all strong, none singled out as core.

species:red-fox.habitatStatement: Open woodland, farmland, tundra and urban-edge habitat across most of North America.
species:red-fox.reading: Open woodland, farmland, grass, shrub and tundra are all strong, none singled out as core; closed forest, towns and wetland moderate.

species:rock-ptarmigan.habitatStatement: Rocky Arctic and alpine tundra, generally more exposed than willow ptarmigan habitat.
species:rock-ptarmigan.reading: Rocky ground and lichen tundra are core; grass tundra strong; shrub (willow ptarmigan's habitat) marginal; forest is not habitat.

species:rosss-goose.habitatStatement: Breeds in the central Canadian Arctic; migrates and winters with snow geese.
species:rosss-goose.reading: In the hunting season, with snow geese (whose published statement names agricultural stopovers and coastal wintering areas): farm fields and wetland are core; water and grass strong.

species:sika-deer.habitatStatement: Introduced; marsh and forest of Maryland and Virginia and some private ranches.
species:sika-deer.reading: Marsh and forest are core; shrub, grass and farmland moderate; the range is drawn tightly because populations are local.

species:snow-goose.habitatStatement: Arctic breeding grounds, agricultural stopovers and coastal wintering areas.
species:snow-goose.reading: In the hunting season: farm fields and coastal marsh are core; water, grass and coastal sea within 10 km of land strong.

species:snowshoe-hare.habitatStatement: Snowshoe hare is a forest species that uses dense conifer, riparian woodland, willow-birch scrub and other habitats with protective understory cover.
species:snowshoe-hare.reading: Dense conifer and willow-birch scrub are core; mixed, open conifer and other forest strong; broadleaf and riparian wetland moderate.

species:striped-skunk.habitatStatement: Farmland, woodland edges and towns across southern Canada and the United States.
species:striped-skunk.reading: Ground where woodland meets field (an edge) is core; farmland, grass, open woodland and towns strong.

species:surf-scoter.habitatStatement: Breeds in northern boreal wetlands and winters on coastal waters.
species:surf-scoter.reading: In the hunting season: coastal sea within 15 km of land is core; inland water moderate.

species:swamp-rabbit.habitatStatement: Bottomland swamps and river floodplains of the south-central United States.
species:swamp-rabbit.reading: Swamp or floodplain water is required; wetland and bottomland broadleaf forest are core; other forest strong.

species:tundra-swan.habitatStatement: Breeds on Arctic tundra and winters on large wetlands and coasts.
species:tundra-swan.reading: In the hunting season: large wetlands and open water are core; coastal sea within 10 km of land strong.

species:virginia-opossum.habitatStatement: Woodland, farmland and towns across the eastern United States and southern Ontario.
species:virginia-opossum.reading: Woodland, farmland and towns are all strong, none singled out as core; conifer, shrub, grass and wetland moderate.

species:white-tailed-deer.habitatStatement: Ontario deer use forest, edge and agricultural landscapes. Winter severity strongly affects population growth and northern range, so broad range should not be read as exact local presence.
species:white-tailed-deer.reading: Ground where forest meets farmland (an edge) is core; broadleaf and mixed forest, farmland and shrub strong; conifer, grass and wetland moderate. Winter severity is not modelled; the range carries it only as far as records do.

species:white-tailed-jackrabbit.habitatStatement: Open prairie, sagebrush and grassland of the northern Great Plains and interior West.
species:white-tailed-jackrabbit.reading: Prairie grass and sagebrush are core; farmland moderate; woodland marginal.

species:white-tailed-ptarmigan.habitatStatement: Alpine tundra above the treeline in western mountains from Alaska to New Mexico.
species:white-tailed-ptarmigan.reading: Mountain terrain is required (local relief); alpine grass, tundra, rock and low willow are core; snowfields moderate; forest (below the treeline) marginal.

species:white-winged-scoter.habitatStatement: Breeds on northern lakes and winters on coastal waters and the Great Lakes.
species:white-winged-scoter.reading: In the hunting season: coastal sea within 20 km of land is core; large lakes strong.

species:wild-boar.habitatStatement: Introduced; feral populations across much of the southern United States, and invasive wild pigs in parts of the Canadian Prairies.
species:wild-boar.reading: The published statement says where, not in what habitat, so no habitat class is assigned: the surface is the known distribution, shaded evenly. A sourced habitat statement would promote it to range and habitat without renderer change.

species:wolverine.habitatStatement: Remote boreal forest, tundra and mountains of northern and western North America.
species:wolverine.reading: Boreal conifer, tundra, alpine and mountain ground are all strong, none singled out as core; towns and farmland are not habitat (remote).

species:woodchuck.habitatStatement: Fields, meadows and forest edges across eastern North America and much of Canada.
species:woodchuck.reading: Ground where forest meets field (an edge) is core; fields and meadows strong; open woodland and shrub moderate.
